title: Jack Bui Lab – Jack Bui Lab
headings: Understanding the dynamic conversation between tumors and the immune system.
text: Bui Lab Dr. Jack Bui Principal Investigator & Professor Department of Pathology – UCSD Understanding the dynamic conversation between tumors and the immune system. Our lab studies immune responses to tumors using animal and human models. We focus on both the tumor cell and immune cells and how each modifies the behavior of the other. The intricate communication and complex counter-regulation evident within the tumor microenvironment provides fertile grounds for discovery and intervention. Our journey has also taken us to studying stem cells, hematopoiesis, cytokine biology, wound healing, and microplastics. Research The Bui Lab investigates several areas including: Cancer Immunology Hematopoiesis Innate Immunity Current projects include the role of the innate cytokine IL-17D in skin inflammation and wound healing, how interferons regulate cancer stem cells and hematopoiesis, how co-receptors such as PD1 and CTLA4 limit tumor and pathogen immunity, how NK cells influence pregnancy and placental biology, and how microplastics affect macrophages. text: Dr. Bui studies how to initiate innate immune responses to cancer. His basic research lab uses mouse and human model systems to elucidate genes involved in tumor rejection. Dr. Bui also directs Clinical Flow Cytometry, Diagnostic Immunology, and Stem Cell Processing. His clinical interests include bone marrow transplantation, stem cell regeneration, and autoimmune disease.
